articles.title: Mikel Arteta, Xabi Alonso and Andoni Iraola started their paths to the top at Antiguoko: 'If I really think about it, it's absolutely crazy'
articles.summary: Born within 15 miles of each other and only seven months apart, the managers of Arsenal, Chelsea and Liverpool are all products of Antiguoko; Sky Sports visited the tiny Basque club to hear how it all began for Mikel Arteta, Xabi Alonso and Andoni Iraola
articles.body:
"The centre circle was just over there," says Roberto Montiel, the club's long-serving coach and vice-president, as he takes a seat in what is now a public park. He rubs his thumb and forefinger together as he recalls the texture of the old playing surface.

"The pitch wasn't like the new one up there. It was smaller and made of small stones, like gravel. The balls weren't like the ones now either. When they got wet, they became heavy. You would slip and slide, and if you fell, you'd end up with a terrible scrape."

The games played here by this neighbourhood club's celebrated alumni are the stuff of local legend.

"Even then you could see their vision for the game," adds Montiel.

"On this pitch made of gravel, trying to pass those balls when it was raining, with puddles all over the place, with everything getting dirty. Honestly, it was something special to watch. The teams from those '81 and '82 generations were incredible."

Arteta and Iraola played in the latter age group; Alonso the former. "It was like a national team of the best players in the area and it made us an unbeatable team," says Alvaro Parra, a former Antiguoko team-mate and close friend of Arteta's.

"I remember games against Real Sociedad that were so easy. They would come to play us and we would beat them 5-0. Athletic Club would come and we would beat them as well. We won all the leagues. The team became known as the Basque Dream Team."

The club continues to turn out talent. Over at their offices, a mile further into town, near Ondarreta beach, Montiel jokes that they need more wall space to continue displaying signed shirts from a list of top-division graduates that now runs to more than 40 names.

Those of Arteta, Alonso and Iraola hold pride of place.

Their former colleagues are used to their success. But it remains a source of wonder, even to them, that these three Antiguoko players, born within 15 miles of each other, only seven months apart, in Gipuzkoa, the smallest province in Spain, have come this far.

"If I really think about it, it's absolutely crazy that our three friends are managing these Premier League teams," says Parra. "Sometimes I turn on the TV and say, 'Oh, it's Mikel! Oh, it's Xabi! What's happened here?'" adds Mikel Yanguas, another old team-mate.

Arteta: 'He was like a predator on the pitch'

Arteta was the pick of them growing up. "He had something different," says Yanguas, who played as a striker. "He was small but very technical and very clever. He played right behind me and he was always thinking about his next pass. I just needed to run."

Yanguas, who later moved to Barcelona's La Masia academy with Arteta, jokes that his old team-mate made him look better than he was. Parra, a former centre-back, feels similarly. "I just had to pass the ball to Mikel Arteta. Mikel Arteta to Yanguas. Goal."

Montiel is full of stories, many of them set on the old gravel pitch, and many of which highlight Arteta's intelligence, even as a boy. "The one I like to tell, and the one that stays with me most, shows that he was a player who was so alert to everything," he says.

"It was right over there, in midfield. The referee blew for a drop ball, and just as he let it bounce, Arteta flicked it away with the outside of his boot and hit a long pass across the pitch for a team-mate who was on his own to score - and that was against Real Sociedad."

There was an edge to Arteta too - even when playing up a year with Alonso. "He had a real competitive look about him," adds Montiel.

"He was super-attentive to everything you said. He showed an interest in everything. And then, when he went on the pitch, he was a predator. And that was against players a year older. I don't even need to tell you what he was like against players of his own age."

Arteta's competitiveness is one of his defining qualities as a manager. It was evident off the pitch as well as on it growing up.

Montiel remembers Arteta sliding, Jurgen Klinsmann-style, down the hallway of his house in Liverpool after beating him at PlayStation during a visit while he was at Everton.

"Whatever game you played with him, you would always lose," adds Parra. "If you played PlayStation, you would lose. If you played ping pong, you would lose. He was very, very competitive. If you beat him at anything, he would get angry and go home."

Parra chuckles as he utters the last line. He and Arteta were otherwise inseparable, their friendship, and holidays together, continuing even after his career took him abroad.

"After the year he made his debut with Paris Saint-Germain, he called me and said, 'Alvaro, pack your suitcase, we're going to Marbella.'" Parra has no photographs of that trip, lamentably. But he reaches for his phone and flicks through a selection of others.

Parra cherishes the memories. But Arteta, he stresses, was also organised and disciplined, in all aspects of his life, including his studies. "His parents instilled that in him."

Those qualities helped when he made the move to Barcelona aged only 15. Yanguas, although similarly talented according to those who first spotted him playing on La Concha beach with Arteta, never settled and returned home the following year.

"Mikel had a better capacity to adapt," he says. "He was quickly speaking to the other people at La Masia. I think he demonstrated that in other countries too, in France, in Scotland, in England. He always had the ability to adapt to any environment."

Iraola: 'A great team-mate and quiet leader'

Back in Berio, we have moved up the slope from the site of Antiguoko's old pitch to their new one, where an U16s team are being put through their paces under the midday sun.

"This is a very good group," says Montiel, before gesturing towards a slight figure in central midfield who stands out for his technical quality. "He had an offer from Real Sociedad but preferred to stay with us," he adds, with more than a hint of pride.

Real Sociedad and Athletic are signing Antiguoko players at ever-younger ages, Montiel says. But for some, the education on offer at Antiguoko is reason to stay. The coach overseeing this session, Iñigo Iraola, cousin of Andoni, is certainly from good footballing stock.

Like the older Iraola, who returned to Antiguoko as a coach while studying for his badges following his playing career, Iñigo came through the club's youth ranks as a player.

"The first game I ever watched was here in Berio, when Andoni came back with Athletic Club as an U18," he says. "From then on I always saw him as a role model and an example to follow."

He remembers Andoni taking him to buy his first pair of football boots. "They were Adidas boots," he says, smiling. "I went to buy them with him on my birthday here in San Sebastian. He was already playing for Athletic, so it was special for me to go with him."

Iraola is remembered differently to Arteta as a boy at Antiguoko.

"Mikel was captain of the team, he took responsibility," says Parra. "Andoni was more introverted, but at the same time he had incredible ability, and even if he was quieter, he was always a fun and polite guy, a great team-mate, and popular in the group."

"He was one of my favourites," adds Montiel. "Playing out wide, he didn't get as many touches as those in the centre, but every time he got to the byline, he would beat two or three players, make a pass and we'd score. He could work wonders with the ball."

He had the same competitive streak as Arteta. And although he was more reserved, as Parra explains, he had his moments.

"In our team, he played as a right winger and had a really important role," says Parra. "But when he went to Athletic, their manager Ernesto Valverde moved him to full-back.

"At first, he didn't like it at all. He even got angry, asking, 'Why are you putting me in defence?' But Valverde knew he was going to be an incredible full-back because he had the quality and the ability to take on players and get all the way up the pitch."

Iraola's leadership abilities emerged later, first as captain of Athletic, where he ended up making 510 appearances, then as a manager.

"One thing I really admire about Andoni is the kind of leader he is," says his cousin. "He isn't going to raise his voice above everyone else. He's a quieter, understated kind of leader who has more of an impact through the example he sets his players every day."

Ignacio Azpilicueta likes to joke that he had the best view in football.

As the central defender who occupied the space directly behind Alonso at Antiguoko, he enjoyed a front-row seat as his teenaged team-mate began to find his passing range.

"He played as the midfield pivot right in front of me, so I had the privilege of seeing Xabi's best passes from my position, right at the point when he developed the physical power and ball-striking ability that he went on to show for so many years."

Alonso had always been a good player. "He won the ball back a lot, played with two feet, and all of his passes were good," says Montiel. Azpilicueta recalls friends commenting on Alonso's ability during intra-school tournaments on La Concha beach.

He would come alive on the pitch. "He was really passionate," says Yanguas. "He really lived the game." But starting out at Antiguoko, few felt stardom beckoned for him.

"I remember our first sessions together and I would say I don't remember feeling that he was going to become the football star he is today," says Azpilicueta, who is no relation to the former Chelsea defender of the same name but had a good career of his own.

"He had a good touch, but physically he wasn't by any means the biggest or the strongest or the quickest. It took him a while to grow."

His trajectory, both physically and in terms of his career, changed in his U17 year. "I would say that was the moment when he really took off," says Azpilicueta. "He'd always had that intelligence, but now it was accompanied by that physical development."

"At that age, you could see he was going to be a first division player," says Parra. "Maybe not that he was going to win the Champions League, but you could see was going to be a top-level player."

According to Azpilicueta, he also benefitted from the qualities of humility and intelligence evident in Arteta and Iraola.

"I would say he was a very normal kid, like the rest of us. He didn't stand out in any particular way. He had a sense of humour. He was a good friend to his friends. But above all, he was very intelligent. He always made good decisions, on and off the pitch.

"I would say that has been a big part of his success."

So how does this little club do it? Arteta, Alonso and Iraola are of course their best-known graduates but more recent ones include Arsenal's Martin Zubimendi, their second World Cup winner after Alonso, and Rayo Vallecano boss Iñigo Perez.

Some point to the club's scouting in the area - "Oscar Landa, our sporting director, has a 95 per cent success rate," says Montiel - others to the atmosphere created by the longevity and commitment of their staff. But it usually comes back to the same thing.

"We've never changed the DNA of Antiguoko," says Montiel. "Competitive instinct, intensity and sporting discipline are non-negotiable." It is surely no coincidence that his old mentee Arteta uses that same term in reference to his managerial philosophy.

"We try to instil the values of sacrifice, discipline, hard work, teamwork and competitiveness," adds Iñigo Iraola. "I think it also reflects what the Basque player is: dedicated and committed to working hard every day. I think that's what makes us special."

Arteta, Alonso and Iraola personify those traits, as much managers as they did as players.

"The results should be seen in sporting terms, but also in human terms," says the club's general director Gorka Azpeita. "Beyond the footballing talent they have, it's important to highlight what they're like as people. They should be seen for the values they have, the people they are, and how it's enabled them to get where they are."

The only remaining question, then, is who they will be rooting for when Arteta and Alonso go head to head some 600 miles away in north London on Sunday. "That's like choosing between Mum and Dad," says Azpeita, laughing. "A draw would be perfect."

articles.title: World Cup: Fans shown over 65,000 junk food ads during football matches
articles.summary: New data shows fans were shown more than 28 hours of adverts for unhealthy food and drinks during World Cup matches this summer.
articles.body:
Football fans were shown a "constant bombardment" of advertisements promoting junk food and drinks during matches at the 2026 Fifa World Cup, according to a new study.

Researchers at the University of Bristol and University of Oxford created an AI tool to analyse ads which were visible to television viewers during live play in the tournament's 104 matches, mostly displayed on pitchside advertising boards and around stadiums in the USA, Canada, and Mexico.

They found that logos and products for brands that produce junk food and drinks - defined by the UK government as being high in fat, salt or sugar - were displayed 65,722 times in total.

And the study also found that those adverts were visible for 28.1 hours' time across the tournament, or just over 16% of the total time that matches were being played.

The ads were all shown on the international feed of matches during play - meaning they were visible to every viewer in every country broadcasting matches - and do not include ads shown during pre-match coverage, half-time commercial breaks, or the controversial in-match hydration breaks.

The model used by the researchers estimated that there were an average of 576 visible ads for junk food and drink shown during each individual match.

Coca-Cola had the highest number (21,893), followed by McDonald's (13,915), Powerade (12,777), and Lay's - the crisps manufacturer known as Walkers in the UK - (12,087).

All four brands are official partners of world football governing body Fifa, with the Powerade energy drink owned by the Coca-Cola company.

In response to the findings, Fifa argued that the vast majority of its revenue is put back into football, including on projects promoting health and wellbeing in which thousands of people participate.

A Fifa spokesperson said: "Fifa works with a broad, global portfolio of partners, all of which are subject to its governance and compliance frameworks.

"Fifa's social impact campaigns, including Be Active, delivered messages of unity, inclusion, health and friendship to audiences on an unprecedented scale throughout the World Cup".

BBC Sport also contacted Coca Cola, McDonald's and PepsiCo - which owns Lay's - but did not receive a reply.

The report also analysed other forms of "potentially harmful" advertising, and found that junk food and drink promotion was far more prevalent.

Junk food and drink logos were recorded around seven times more often than those for alcohol and prediction market brands, 10 times more often than those of gambling firms, and almost 25 times more often than cryptocurrency.

"Repeatedly connecting unhealthy food and drink brands with football, excitement and national identity can make these brands familiar and normalise their consumption," the researchers argue.

Since October 2025, foods such as burgers, chips, crisps and drinks with added sugar have been included in a ban on junk food advertising on TV before 9pm in the UK.

But because the advertising shown during matches appears on hoardings, and is at an international event, it falls outside the legislation.

That means viewers seeing ads for burgers, crisps and fizzy drinks during the hours they are theoretically banned, and calls have grown for a more global approach.

"It is definitely a loophole," Greg Fell, president of the Association of Directors of Public Health, told BBC Sport.

"There is acres of evidence demonstrating that governments around the world are legislating very hard at the moment to limit advertising of junk food.

"It requires worldwide collaboration because obesity is a problem everywhere. Advertising is one of the key mechanisms by which harm from obesity happens.

"Obesity is almost the new tobacco - there isn't much difference with the methods the tobacco industry used before they were excluded from advertising.

"A lot of this is targeted at children, because these companies want to grow their markets, and children are the future market."

The UK government recently announced sweeping changes to school dinner rules, banning deep-fried food and increasing the inclusion of fruit, vegetables, fibre and wholegrains, in attempt to tackle childhood obesity.

According to the NHS, data from 2024 showed that 15% of children in the UK were obese, and 26% were overweight.

"We are facing a global crisis of childhood obesity and diet-related disease, yet the world's biggest sporting event is saturated with marketing for unhealthy food and drinks", said Dr Elisa Becker, one of the report's co-authors.

"Sport should be part of the solution to poor health – not one of the world's most powerful advertising platforms for the products driving it."

articles.title: "Uno de los equipos que ha ascendido este año a Primera puede que no exista en dos o tres años"
articles.standfirst: Miguel Ángel Ramírez asegura que "uno de los equipos que ha ascendido ha pedido un préstamo por las cinco temporadas que vienen de derechos de televisión"
articles.summary: Miguel Ángel Ramírez asegura que "uno de los equipos que ha ascendido ha pedido un préstamo por las cinco temporadas que vienen de derechos de televisión"
articles.body: Miguel Ángel Ramírez, presidente de la Unión Deportiva Las Palmas, vaticinó en su participación en el podcast 'Helado Oscuro' la desaparición "en dos o tres años" de uno de los tres equipos que ascendieron a Primera División. La pasada temporada los tres equipos que ascendieron de la LaLiga HyperMotion a la LaLiga EA Sports fueron Racing de Santander, Deportivo de La Coruña y Málaga CF. "No voy a dar un nombre, pero uno de los equipos que ha ascendido este año ha pedido un préstamo por las cinco temporadas que vienen de derechos de televisión. Ese equipo en dos o tres años puede que no exista. Yo eso no lo puedo hacer", comentó el máximo dirigente de la UD Las Palmas. Miguel Ángel Ramírez compartió que "Yeremay no está en la UD Las Palmas porque yo no quise". "Su representante es un enemigo de la Unión Deportiva Las Palmas", denunció el presidente. Ramírez explicó que "a Yeremai se le dijo 'si quieres fichar por la UD Las Palmas, que estamos encantados de ficharte, tienes que cambiar de representante. Él no cambio de representante y se fue al Deportivo de La Coruña". "No hay más mentiras. Yeremai estaba para venir aquí y nosotros estábamos encantados, pero no lo íbamos a hacer con esa persona. Hay representantes que son enemigos nuestros, que nos quitan jugadores, y no queremos hacer negocios con ellos... Esto es una empresa, no nos olvidemos de eso", apuntó. Yeremay Hernández (23 años) fichó en 2017 por el Deportivo tras salir de la cantera del Real Madrid y jugar anteriormente en las categorías inferiores de Las Palmas de 2011 a 2015.

articles.title: Aston Villa: Is Alejandro Garnacho already at crossroads at club?
articles.summary: Alejandro Garnacho joined Aston Villa on loan from Chelsea with a view to kick-starting his career, but his early weeks in the Midlands have been a struggle.
articles.body:
Just like last season, questions are being asked about Alejandro Garnacho.

Two months after joining from Chelsea on an initial loan, the winger has yet to convince Aston Villa boss Unai Emery of his worth.

The Argentina forward has played just 31 minutes for Villa, spread across three substitute appearances.

A 15-minute outing against Hull is the most time he has spent on the pitch in a game.

Garnacho has been an unused substitute for Villa's past four matches , watching from the bench again as they won 3-2 at Tottenham on Saturday.

One goal and four assists in 24 Premier League games for Chelsea last term fell below what the Blues expected from their £40m recruit from Manchester United , so he was allowed to move on.

This campaign is only a month old, but 22-year-old Garnacho could be at a crossroads at Villa Park already.

Emery likes to ease new players into his teams.

Youri Tielemans did not start a Premier League game until November 2023 after joining in the summer, but became an integral part of Emery's machine.

Only Joao Gomes, out of 10 new summer signings, started Villa's opening Premier League game. Just two - Zion Suzuki and Nicolas Jackson - started the next.

Garnacho's situation feels extreme though, having been left on the bench for the Carabao Cup win at Coventry when Emery made seven changes.

Academy product George Hemmings, who joined Villa from Forest as a teenager, has started the season well to earn Emery's full trust and start ahead of Garnacho.

Ibrahim Mbaye, a £47m arrival from Paris St-Germain, made his first Villa start in the 3-1 victory at Coventry and is also preferred to Garnacho for now.

A facial injury in early August hampered Garnacho's pre-season and meant he missed the Super Cup defeat by Paris St-Germain, adding to the complications.

Emery needs his players to understand their roles and his methods before having full faith in them and he expects Garnacho to catch up.

"Continue working. Work, work, train, work," Emery said when asked about Garnacho's absence from the pitch.

"When he can have minutes to play, try to play well. He is progressing, but we have players in front of him now.

"George is playing fantastic. Alysson is also understanding things well and is giving us things I want. [Ibrahim] Mbaye also responded well.

"We want a competitive team and players to compete in the style we have. Garnacho is a little bit behind because of some circumstances we had in pre-season. It is time to be patient for the time he needs."

Garnacho, who first made his name as a livewire teenager, has shown in the past he can torment defences at Premier League level.

He spoke about needing time to adapt to a "different club and a different place" at Chelsea .

A further season of struggle would be a significant setback.

Emery is clearly yet to be convinced by what he sees in training, despite being a long-term Garnacho admirer.

Villa wanted more pace in their side and Crysencio Summerville was considered before he moved to Saudi Arabia's Al-Hilal.

Chelsea's £117m signing of Morgan Rogers from Villa left a gap for Emery to fill and Garnacho was available. A positive relationship between the clubs allowed for easy discussions.

Striker Jackson also joined from Chelsea for a Villa club record £65m and there have been eight deals between the clubs in the past four years.

Garnacho did not train with Xabi Alonso's Chelsea squad before leaving for Villa Park in July.

Roma were interested in the winger, but their loan offer did not suit Chelsea . Instead, Villa's deal gives the Blues the chance to make their money back after last year's outlay.

There is an obligation to buy tied into the loan that is believed to relate to appearances, and it is expected to be achievable - but that does not guarantee anything.

For instance, Harvey Elliott would have triggered a move worth £35m if he made just 10 Premier League appearances last season. As it turned out, the Liverpool loanee - now at Valencia - was used just four times by Villa in the top flight.

Emery did not feel the 23-year-old was good enough and made up his mind not to sign Elliott permanently just a couple of months into the season.

It raised the question for some within the game about whether a loan at Villa should be viewed with caution, and whether other players' careers could be derailed in the way Elliott experienced.

It was accepted that Elliott's options this summer were not as extensive following his season at Villa Park.

Time will tell whether Garnacho faces the same struggles, having experienced his career stalling over the past two years.

He made his Manchester United debut aged 17 and was part of Argentina's Copa America‑winning squad in 2024, but has not added to his eight international caps since November of that year.

The Madrid-born attacker also won the Premier League's goal of the season award in 2023-24 for his overhead kick against Everton while playing for United, but his output for Chelsea was disappointing.

Emery is waiting to see Garnacho fulfil his full potential at Villa, but the winger will have to wait until he gains the coach's trust, and then take his chance.

articles.title: Así fue el cara a cara de Ferrán Torres con la responsable del vídeo viral "Oh, Ferran": "Me salió del alma"
articles.standfirst: El héroe de España en la final del Mundial conoció a Rocío Domingo en El Hormiguero
articles.summary: El héroe de España en la final del Mundial conoció a Rocío Domingo en El Hormiguero
articles.body: Ferran Torres, el autor del gol que proclamó a España campeona del Mundial 2026, habló en el programa 'El Hormiguero' sobre el challenge del "oh, Ferran" que se hizo viral el pasado verano tras el partido de dieciseisavos de final contra Austria. La responsable del vídeo viral es Rocío Domingo, que compartió en su cuenta de TikTok un vídeo citando a varios jugadores de la Selección.. y a Ferran Torres: "El mayor facto del mundial, las cosas como son". "Yo estaba en Estados Unidos en una burbuja, concentrado con la misma gente y al margen de todo. Hasta después de la Rua no me di cuenta del revuelo que estaba generando el vídeo viral de '¡Oh, Ferran!'. La verdad es que me da muchísima vergüenza", le confesó Ferran Torres a Pablo Motos sobre el cómo se enteró de la viralidad del "oh, Ferran". El ex del Barcelona bromeó comentando que "me conocen más por el audio que por el gol". La protagonista original del audio viral del "oh, Ferran" es Rocío Domingo, y 'El Hormiguero' hizo posible el encuentro entre el futbolista la joven. "Hay que tomárselo con humor. Ha sido muy divertido la gente ha disfrutado con el audio, no sólo yo, creo que va a ser recordado... Ya me ha perseguido en el Barça, en el PSG", admitió Ferran Torres. Rocío Domingo reconoció sobra la frase viral "oh, Ferran" que "le salió del alma". "¿Qué tiene Ferran Torres que no tienen los demás? Le da vergüenza a él y le da vergüenza a mí... Es muy buen futbolista", contestó entre risas Rocío.

articles.title: Josh McPake's 'colourful' journey from club-less to Scotland call-up in three years
articles.summary: Three years ago, Josh McPake was without a club. Twenty months ago, he was in the shop window but "no-one wanted him". This week, he's involved in his first Scotland camp. Here, BBC Sport Scotland charts the fall and rise of the winger who's got everyone in the country talking.
articles.body:
Three years ago, Josh McPake was without a club. Twenty months ago, he was in the shop window but "no-one wanted him".

This week, he's involved in his first Scotland camp following a heroic start to life at Hearts, where, to the tune of Abba's Dancing Queen, the supporters sing he is "having the time of his life".

His call-up to Sebastien Poconogli's squad for the upcoming Nations League games caps an eventful few years for the 25-year-old winger.

From Rangers academy's next big thing, to dropping into Scottish League 1 with Stirling Albion, to being shelved at St Johnstone, it's been a colourful - and at times chaotic - career so far.

But, "I wouldn't change my journey for anything," McPake insists.

He now appears at home in Gorgie and many have hopes he will be just as comfortable when he gets the opportunity to represent his country.

His story is one of resilience and patience. And it's paying off.

His story starts like many others, in the Ibrox academy from a young age, where he was awarded player of the year in 2019 by working up through the reserves to the fringes of the first team.

A matter of months after collecting the gong, he was given his first - and only - run-out for Steven Gerrard's side.

His appearance off the bench in Rangers' rout against Gibraltar's St Joseph's in Europa League qualifying was not a sign of things to come, as he was sent out on his first of six loan moves just one month later.

Dundee, Greenock Morton, Harrogate Town, Morecambe, Tranmere Rovers and Queen's Park all had a taste of McPake but nothing permanent was made.

He swiftly became a bit of a football nomad.

While on Tayside, he scored the winner for Scotland Under-19s against Germany, but still he was flung from pillar to post.

On 1 September 2023, he left Rangers and, though he trained with a number of clubs - where he endured some "knocks and setbacks" - he didn't find a home for another near-six months, until Stirling signed him on a short-term deal.

A dunt down to earth, no doubt, but McPake didn't allow any ego to get in his way, as then-Binos boss Darren Young recalled.

"He came into training and he was brilliant - he couldn't have done any more," former Aberdeen midfielder Young told BBC Scotland.

"He worked very, very hard. He helped put balls away after training, he was always doing extra bits of shooting and finishing - I joked to him once or twice, 'if you don't get your finger out then you'll end up back here part-time' but it was one of those where you could see his ability, he was head and shoulders above the guys.

"It was just a case of him then doing it and getting into the kind of situation where a club - and the right club - would come and get him."

He scored on his debut for the League 1 side - though that was little surprise to Young who was left "wondering why he had not been signed up" when he got the move in motion.

"We had an eye on him as he was free but it looked like he was going to sign at a higher level but another player got injured and then the move wasn't going to happen," he explained.

"He sort of found himself in limbo but I think there's a lot of positives that can be learned from that.

"He kind of said, 'well, I don't want to be in this position and I don't want to be back down there again' and the only way to do that is by working hard and working on weaknesses, which he did."

It'll be of no surprise McPake didn't lack anything in the attacking sense. A wee bit of fine tuning on his tracking back was all that was required during his time at Forthbank to fire him back to where he wanted to be.

"I didn't need to tell him how to go by a player and put it in the top corner - he had all that," Young said.

"I was just trying to say if he could fit into the structure here, work as hard at going back as he did forward, then he'd get, hopefully, an opportunity to kick on again.

"Some players don't, some players kind of have that attitude of, 'I can do it going forward, I don't need to do it going back,' but the penny dropped and he realised to improve and progress, that's what he had to add.

"He worked hard for it and he's got what he deserved."

The reward for knuckling down - and dropping down - was a move back to the top flight with St Johnstone - despite suffering relegation with Stirling Albion.

A two-year deal was agreed but he failed to force his way into Craig Levein's team, and had similar struggles when Simo Valakari took over in October 2024.

His mettle was being pushed to the max yet again.

The Finn revealed last year , external that McPake was made available in the winter transfer window while Saints were fighting for their Premiership life, but they "couldn't find him any clubs".

"We made Josh available in January and offered him to many clubs because he needed to play," Valakari said.

"The truth is, nobody wanted him. We couldn't find him any clubs.

"And, for me, that was the wake-up call for Josh. That was when he decided things had to change.

"If things had stayed the way they were then football was done for him. He would have had to go and get a normal life."

McPake started his first Premiership game for St Johnstone in the first of their five post-split games and kept his place until the end of the season as he registered three assists.

Saints were ultimately relegated but it set him up for the season of his dreams.

He set the tone for the Championship campaign he dominated with a hat-trick on the opening weekend against title rivals Partick Thistle.

In the second tier, his blistering pace, immense physicality and dancing feet were flung back into the spotlight. His eye for a goal - 16 all told in the division - was evident, too.

Such qualities caught the attention of then Premiership leaders Hearts, who agreed a pre-contract back in January.

But there was no head-turn from the winger, who remained fully focused on repaying the club who resurrected his career by ensuring they would be an opponent of his this season.

He ended the campaign with the mantelpiece packed with trophies and, while the personal accolades were appreciated, it was all about the Championship winners' medal for Tynecastle-bound McPake.

Back to the big time with ‘more to give’

Ensuring adversity remained an ever present in his tale, the footballing gods - seemingly - threw another curveball McPake's way.

Though Derek McInnes was in charge when he agreed the move, the head coach had headed for Rangers by the time he got going in Gorgie.

But, despite sitting out the Champions League qualifiers against Sturm Graz and the first league game of the season under Wouter Vrancken, the Belgian has quickly found out why Hearts snapped up the Saints showman when they did.

With eight goal involvements in 11 games - his best contribution a goal and assist in the Edinburgh derby - he has made the step back up to the Premiership a seamless one and, as such, made it nigh impossible for Pocognoli to leave him out of his plans.

"I've loved every part of the journey," McPake said after answering his country's call.

"Personally, I feel I needed those experiences to become the player I am now.

"There were a lot of setbacks but going down the levels, proving myself and working my way back up taught me a lot.

"If you want something enough and work hard for it, you can achieve it.

"I don't want to stop here. I feel I've still got more to give and I'll continue working hard to show what I can do."

articles.title: Félix Correia hace cuentas
articles.standfirst: El portugués se marca 10 contribuciones de gol como objetivo, quiere volver a la selección y asentar al Sevilla en LaLiga
articles.summary: El portugués se marca 10 contribuciones de gol como objetivo, quiere volver a la selección y asentar al Sevilla en LaLiga
articles.body: Félix Correia es uno de los debutantes esta temporada con la camiseta del Sevilla. El portugués ha sido titular en los tres últimos partidos de LaLiga y en la útlima derrota ante el Barcelona, asistió a Fofana para adelantar a los andaluces en el marcador. Es precisamente en este tipo de escenarios donde el jugador se siente cómodo: desde muy joven ha aprendido a desenvolverse en contextos de alta presión. En el último día del pasado mercado de fichajes, la entidad hispalense alcanzaba un acuerdo con el Lille para la cesión con opción de compra del futbolista de 25 años. Con experiencia en Portugal, Inglaterra, Italia y Francia, el Sevilla se presentó como una oportunidad especialmente atractiva para un Félix Correia que desde hace tiempo tenía el sueño de jugar en España. El extremo se ha marcado para esta temporada una meta concreta: alcanzar, al menos, los 10 contribuciones en LaLiga, sumando ambas contribuciones directas al gol. Su primer pase de gol frente al Barcelona supone el punto de partida de ese reto personal. El portugués ha ido de menos a más desde que debutase frente al Valencia. Considera que el estilo del Sevilla puede potenciar sus características como jugador haciendo lo que le pide Luis García Plaza. En ataque, el entrenador le pide ser objetivo, vertical y pragmático a la hora de atacar la portería rival; en defensa, compromiso y capacidad para ayudar al equipo. Una exigencia a la que ya se había acostumbrado la pasada temporada durante su etapa en el Lille. Además de alcanzar la cifra de 10 contribuciones directas de gol -goles y asistencias- en la competición, Félix Correia confía también en que puede contribuir a que el Sevilla complete una temporada más tranquila en LaLiga. Espera que el torneo español sea un buen escaparate para volver a entrar también en los planes de la selección portuguesa, después de haber llegado a estar preconvocado durante su etapa en el Lille.

articles.title: Women's Super League: Does WSL have a homegrown problem?
articles.summary: The London City Lionesses raised eyebrows with no English players in their starting line-up against Manchester United, but is there a wider trend?
articles.body:
When London City Lionesses beat Manchester United on the opening night of the 2025-26 season, it suggested times were changing in the English women's game.

For some, that had become clear about an hour before kick-off in Bromley when the team news revealed a starting XI without any English players - the first time a Women's Super League side had done so on the first day of the season.

Two days later it happened again, when Scotland striker Kirsty Hanson was the only British player to start for Tottenham in their win over West Ham.

Both instances speak to the increasing ability of WSL clubs to attract top talents from across the globe, creating a league many now view as the world's best.

But, with the Women's Champions League returning this week, is what's good for the WSL good for homegrown players, and by extension the home nations?

Or is it, as The Guardian's Tom Garry puts it, "alarming" for the hopes of the home nations?

Arsenal v HB Koge, Women's Champions League

Listen to BBC Radio 5 Live commentary and follow text updates of the matches featuring English teams on the BBC Sport website as the Women's Champions League returns

Ten years ago when current champions Manchester City last won the WSL title, they did so with an all-British starting line-up.

In 2018, the WSL went fully professional, the subsequent success of the Lionesses in the 2020s rapidly grew the game's audience and revenues have increased accordingly.

As a result, clubs have expanded their scouting pool and been able to attract players from a wider variety of nationalities - with transfer fees exploding since the turn of the decade.

Over recent windows, WSL clubs have recruited heavily from Germany and Sweden, while two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas exchanged the trophies of Barcelona for big-spending London City this summer.

The proliferation of players from Japan and Australia also highlights the WSL's attractiveness for those at the top of the game as those clubs with the deepest pockets pack their squads with players from across the globe.

"Our league has grown significantly and attracted world class athletes from all over the world," says Birmingham City manager Amy Merricks. "Unfortunately that blocks some of the pathways for the youngsters coming through.

"We need [this] talent in our league because our league is growing, but at the same time we have got to try and address this issue."

Looking at the proportion of homegrown players (English, Scottish, Welsh and Northern Irish) to start 11 or more matches, half of a WSL season, the data shows a steady decline over the past three seasons to under a third.

The first three weeks of 2026-27 have offered a bump on last season, but that can partly be attributed to the WSL's expansion from 12 teams to 14 teams and the greater proportion of homegrown talent in the promoted trio of Birmingham City, Crystal Palace and Charlton Athletic.

It is a downward trend that is not mirrored across other major European leagues.

For 2025-26, 61% of those to start half or more of Premiere Ligue matches in France were French, 63% of those in Frauen Bundesliga games were German, and 69% of Liga F players in Spain were Spanish.

And, while WSL managers say they appreciate the importance of cultivating homegrown talent, the reality of the job ensures it is not their first priority.

"The club has a responsibility to raise young players, give our own talents possibilities to be in the squad and compete every week," says Manchester City boss Andree Jeglertz.

"But when it comes to team selection, I always need to pick the team that gives us the best chance of winning the game. If that contains eight young and promising English players or zero, I don't care. I just want to win the game."

Ellen White and Ben Haines discuss homegrown WSL players on the Women's Football Weekly

Superstar-led London City live up to hype as Man Utd suffer

What is the potential impact on the national team?

It feels like a crossroads has been reached between clubs wanting to be competitive, the WSL continuing to grow, and the need to regenerate an England squad that has not changed much over the past three major tournaments.

After all, England are the two-time European champions but seven of the team that started against Spain in June also played in the Euro 2022 final against Germany - while two of the remaining starters in this year's game were on the bench four years ago.

Sarina Wiegman's side were outclassed in Majorca, losing 4-0 to miss out on automatic qualification for the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil. They must now navigate two rounds of play-off matches, starting against Greece next month.

Discussions on England's future is pertinent given the biennial Women's Under-20s World Cup is ongoing in Poland.

Last Thursday, Lydia Bedford's young side were dismissed 3-0 from the last 16 by Nigeria, albeit with the caveat a number of players such as US-based Erica Meg Parkinson and Laila Harbert were not released by their clubs to play.

Nevertheless, in 2022 and 2024, like the other home nations, they did not even qualify.

It is a far cry from the class of 2018 where the likes of Alessia Russo, Lauren Hemp and Georgia Stanway led the Lionesses to third place in the Under-20s World Cup, setting the tone for the incredible subsequent success.

Wiegman has handed debuts to 21 players since her arrival in September 2021, but only Lauren James, Hannah Hampton and Lucia Kendall have become established starters.

When England kick off in Crete on Friday, 5 October (20:00 BST), it is likely to be the same faces once again.

To try and facilitate the pathway to top level football for young academy players, Football Association rules require WSL sides to include eight homegrown players in their squad lists.

The quota for WSL 2 clubs is higher and works on a sliding scale depending on squad size.

Former England striker Ellen White told the Women's Football Weekly podcast this was insufficient, saying: "We should be updating that quota of eight players, tweaking it to best help and complement our international structure, our homegrown talent."

"I would love to see them go much further - something mandated, a minimum on the pitch at any one time," the Guardian's Garry told BBC Women's Football Weekly. "London City's line-up was alarming.

"It's great for the product over here, but will we see pain in 15 years' time if England are struggling to go deep in major tournaments because we're not developing players?"

Last month, the FA approved a controversial plan to allow some WSL academy sides to play in the National League from 2027-28, saying it would "strengthen the women's football pyramid, raise standards across the league, and improve the development pathway for young players".

The FA believes this reform will address the relative lack of competitive minutes young English players receive.

Chelsea have already confirmed they plan to enter an academy side in the third tier and Manchester City women's managing director Charlotte O'Neill has previously said she would want to enter a team too.

articles.title: La denuncia el técnico del Wanderers al Real Madrid antes de la final de la intercontinental sub 20
articles.standfirst: Felipe Salinas explicó que les llevaron al museo del Bernabéu y les tuvieron más de una hora caminando el día anterior
articles.summary: Felipe Salinas explicó que les llevaron al museo y les tuvieron
articles.body: El Real Madrid se proclamó campeón de la Copa Intercontinental sub 20 el pasado sábado en el Santiago Bernabéu ante el Santiago Wanderers (3-1) y apenas unos días después el entrenador del conjunto chileno ha desvelado en TNT Sports algunas de las, a su juicio, artimañas del club blanco para desgastarles. El día de antes, de forma conjunta ambos equipos, pasearon por todo el Santiago Bernabéu para que los chilenos se familiarizasen con el campo y también conociesen el museo y las entrañas del recinto. Algo que, sin embargo, no gustó nada a Felipe Salinas, técnico del Wanderers. "Nos tuvieron caminando más de una hora por todo el estadio", explica. "Yo le dije al chico que iba con nosotros que hasta cuándo nos iba a tener caminando, que esta era muy vieja. Mañana jugamos, corta el tour, no hay nada más que ver”, explica Salinas con respecto a la actividad que programó el Real Madrid el día de antes. De hecho, el preparador chileno insistió en que el punto físico fue clave en la final, no centrándose únicamente en lo sucedido el día anterior, sino poniendo el foco en el escenario, el rival o el viaje. "Fue complicado, nosotros teníamos que estar en un gran punto físico para rendir a estos niveles, aparte de que el viaje fue largo, todo lo que supuso llegar hasta allí…", contó. Y, por último, puso el foco en el colegiado, el polaco Damian Sylwestrzak. "No hablaba en inglés, de repente te contestaba en polaco o en alemán. No sabíamos qué hacerle para que nos entendiese. Hubo cosas que estaban fuera de nuestra alcance...", recordó. Una afirmación que también respaldó el guardameta del equipo, Fabiano Avello, horas después del choque. "Teníamos cero comunicación con el árbitro. Los jugadores del Real Madrid tenían un inglés muy fluido, entonces ellos hablaban con el juez y nosotros no pasábamos de las dos palabras. Además, cuando tratábamos de charlar con el árbitro, él nos sacaba. En ese sentido fue una gran desventaja, no sabíamos lo que nos decía el árbitro", afirmó el guardameta.

articles.title: El futbolista internacional con Inglaterra aplastado por una aplanadora: "Es horrible volver a verlo"
articles.summary: El futbolista Andros Townsend, exjugador de Tottenham 13 veces internacional con Inglaterra, fue aplastado por una aplanadora para el mantenimiento del césped mientras calentaba durante el descanso del partido entre PT Prachuap y Pattani en la Thai Premier League.
articles.body: El futbolista Andros Townsend, exjugador de Tottenham 13 veces internacional con Inglaterra, fue aplastado por una aplanadora para el mantenimiento del césped mientras calentaba durante el descanso del partido entre PT Prachuap y Pattani en la Thai Premier League. "Pensé que se me iba a romper el tobillo", le explicó Andros Townsend a Piers Morgan en 'Football Uncensored', hablando por primera vez sobre el "aterrador" momento en el que fue atropellado la máquina en Tailandia. Towsend, que sólo sufrió "golpes y magulladuras", explicó que "No lo vi venir. Ocurrió en el descanso, cuando salíamos a calentar. Vi dos rodillos a ambos lados del campo. Recuerdo haber pensado: "Nunca había visto algo así en mi carrera, ¿qué están haciendo?". Pero nos llamaron para calentar. No le di mayor importancia. La siguiente vez que lo vi fue cuando estaba literalmente debajo de él y, afortunadamente, no hubo daños graves. Un par de golpes y moratones, pero por suerte logré salir ileso". "Cada vez que veo las imágenes, me estremezco; no doy crédito. Cuando se las envié a mis hijos, pensaron que era inteligencia artificial. Literalmente, tuve que explicarles durante 10 minutos que era real... Es horrible volver a verlo y pensar en lo que podría haber pasado, pero, como dije, tuve la suerte de caer al suelo en el momento justo, así que no se me rompió nada cuando la apisonadora pasó por encima de mí. Y hoy estoy aquí para reírme y contar la historia", se sinceró. El propio Towsen compartió una imagen del vídeo bromeando: "Resulta que jugar fuera contra el Stoke no fue tan malo después de todo".

articles.title: Sheffield FC: BBC podcast goes behind the scenes at 'world's oldest football club'
articles.summary: A new BBC podcast Mud, Sweat and Cheers: Trouble at the Bottom – Sheffield FC goes behind the scenes on an extraordinary season at the world's oldest football club.
articles.body:
A football club at the heart of a tug-of-war between a Qatari-backed venture capital firm and a rock star probably isn't that unusual nowadays.

This is the position that Sheffield FC, founded in 1857 and widely considered the world's oldest football club, were in earlier this year.

Mud, Sweat and Cheers: Trouble at the Bottom – Sheffield FC, a six-part podcast series from BBC Local and BBC Radio Sheffield and hosted by Sheffield singer-songwriter Self Esteem, goes behind the scenes during an extraordinary season for an extraordinary club.

'Only Sheffield could invent football and build a car park on it'

The Club, as they're aptly nicknamed given their historic place in the sport, helped to underpin many of the laws of the modern game with the 'Sheffield Rules' and are one of just two clubs to have been awarded Fifa's prestigious Order of Merit, alongside 15-time European Cup winners Real Madrid.

Interest in the club from Qatar isn't actually anything new, a delegation from the country visited in 2017 in the build up to hosting the 2022 World Cup.

Despite Yorkshire AI Labs, backed by money from the Middle East country, saying they had plans to build a 15,000-seat stadium and a football museum it was Jon McClure, lead singer of Sheffield indie band Reverend and the Makers, who became chairman in March.

McClure is honest and up front about the goals for a club who might be the oldest in the world but have never played in the Football League and whose best FA Cup runs were reaching the fourth round in 1879 and 1880.

"This is not Wrexham. I'm not Ryan Reynolds. Let's get it clear, I'm in an indie band. I know my place in this world," McClure told BBC Radio Sheffield in March.

"I've taken a lot of advice from football people. I'm not a football person, and I won't be involved in football stuff."

In recent years Hollywood actors Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac have helped Wrexham soar through the divisions from the National League up to the Championship.

This might not be Wrexham but McClure, who has also taken over at the club's women's side who play in the fourth tier, has plans for a football academy, eSports hub, national football festival, clothing brand, visitor centre, TV show and getting the club back playing in the city of their and the wider game's birth.

Since 2001 they have played at the Coach and Horses Ground (behind, unsurprisingly, the Coach and Horses pub) in Dronfield, North Derbyshire.

The ground's seen better days, with one female supporter telling the podcast the women's toilets are "disgusting".

"I think everybody wants the club back in the city, but there's only Sheffield that could invent football and build a B&Q car park on it," McClure says in relation to the site of their original home now being occupied by a DIY shop.

With the Club challenging to go up from the Northern Counties East League Premier Division at the back end of the 2025-26 campaign McClure offers free entry to under-16s to try and boost the atmosphere.

"We're pushing for promotion. Obviously, we've got this under-16s come for nowt," he says.

"They're good kids. I've said to them overnight, 'listen, lads, we need more noise out of you'.

"They were a bit quiet. So I said, 'look, if you bring a drum, I'll buy you all a pie'. So I owe them all a pie. Well, a fair trade's no robbery, is it?"

However as good as McClure's intentions might be, not everyone is delighted with the new fans.

One complains about the abuse of players and an announcement is read out over the Tannoy at one game asking them to "refrain from throwing drinks" after a supporter is drenched in lemonade.

The engineer who is a goalscoring machine

The push for an immediate return to the eighth tier is spearheaded by striker Alex Hardwick.

Off the field, Hardwick, like the rest of his team-mates, has another job. His though is a little more unusual than others.

"I'm a design engineer here at the AMRC (advanced manufacturing research centre). I work in a design and prototyping building. I work on a range of different projects, which range from nuclear to automotive," he says.

When he isn't busy with his day job or plundering goals, Hardwick is always willing to help out if one of the lads has an issue with their car and adds that a couple of them "do not know their way around an engine".

Boss Vill Powell acknowledges Hardwick "brings a different dynamic to the dressing room, in terms of his conversation, in terms of his banter, in terms of how he is in general".

Watching on from the stands, hopefully not soaked in lemonade, his grandparents are his number one fans.

"I just love it. I enjoy it. I get disappointed when he can't get a goal," his grandma says.

"We encourage him all the time. I don't disappoint him. Marks out of 10? Yeah, I give him 9.5," his grandad adds.

McClure feels that the Club and the city itself have not done enough to celebrate their role in the history of football.

"For far too long now this city has not shouted about itself. It's enough now," he said.

"Now's our time to stand up and say this city's brilliant.

"We invented this game, and this club invented this game, and we're going to celebrate that."

It's a sentiment shared by the fans, with one saying "if the first club in the world was based in Manchester, it would be all over everywhere. If it was in London, it would be all over everywhere. We do nothing about it" while another adds "I certainly believe Sheffield Club should be held in higher esteem".

Like anyone involved in football management and administration one thing McClure wants more than anything else now is something the world's oldest football club knows all about. Time.

Upon taking over he said: "Judge it in a year. If it's not tangibly in a better place than it is now, come and see me at a match and discuss why you think that's not the case."

articles.title: John Egan: Republic of Ireland's defender's late career resurgence back to Premier League
articles.summary: BBC Sport NI looks at Republic of Ireland centre-back's John Egan's rise back to the Premier League with Hull City and the international set-up under Heimir Hallgrimsson.
articles.body:
Just 18 months ago a 31-year-old John Egan was struggling for minutes off the bench for promotion-chasing Burnley and decided to make a January switch to fellow Championship side Hull City.

Fast forward to the present day and Egan is a Premier League regular for the Tigers, who have taken everyone by surprise upon their return to the top flight.

It's been quite a turnaround for the now 33-year-old, who probably thought his last Premier League appearance had already come, when he was taken off on a stretcher with a season-ending Achilles injury when playing for Sheffield United against West Ham in September 2023.

Egan has quietly rebuilt his career after being released by the Blades, first with the Clarets before finding a home at Hull after joining in 2024.

He signed a new two-year deal earlier this month, has played five of their league games and has even forced his way back into the Republic of Ireland squad.

His late career resurgence back to the Premier League is a story of perseverance and unwavering belief despite considerable adversity.

Hallgrimsson spoke to players individually about Israel games

Coleman not included in Republic of Ireland squad

Hull move catalyst for upturn in fortunes

Egan made 208 appearances for Sheffield United during his six seasons with the club, winning promotion to the Premier League with them in 2019 and 2023.

He was named club captain in the summer of 2023, but would play his last game for the Blades in September that same year as an Achilles injury curtailed his Premier League return and kept him out for close to 10 months.

The defender's contract expired the following summer and the club decided not to renew the deal, leaving Egan hurt and in the lurch as he tried to battle back from that serious injury and continue his career.

He went on trial to Burnley and West Ham, with then Clarets boss Scott Parker seeing enough from the experienced centre-back to offer him a one-year deal with the club seeking a quick return to the top flight after relegation the previous season.

With Burnley then getting off to a flying start in the Championship, Egan, who was working back to full fitness, was restricted to just seven appearances and decided to swap a promotion push at Turf Moor for a relegation battle with Hull just five months later.

He signed an 18-month deal and was thrown straight in, completing his first 90 minutes in over a year, coincidentally against Burnley in a 2-0 loss in February.

The Kerry native would go on to make 10 more appearances as Hull stayed up on goal difference on the final day.

Manager Sergej Jakirovic then came in and transformed the club the following campaign, with a fully-fit Egan a key player in their success.

He played 48 times as Hull sneaked into the play-offs and then beat Middlesborough in the final to return to the Premier League for the first time since 2017.

Egan picked up where he left off last season in the top flight this term, as evidenced by his performance in the opening day 2-0 victory over Manchester United.

He made 18 clearances against the Red Devils and has since helped the Tigers keep clean sheets against Coventry and Aston Villa before they earned a point against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge and lost narrowly against Newcastle.

It's been a dream return to the top flight for Hull and Egan, who have shown they are up for the fight in the battle to stay in the league.

Republic of Ireland recall two years on and eyeing up more caps

Egan's form at Hull helped him to earn an international recall with the Republic of Ireland in October last year, after two years without a call-up.

Previously an automatic starter, the rise of the likes of Nathan Collins, Dara O'Shea and Jake O'Brien have pushed him down the pecking order and he has played a bit-part role under Heimir Hallgrimsson.

Egan came off the bench for the closing stages of the 1-0 defeat against Portugal and was then on the bench for the subsequent wins against Armenia, Portugal and famously Hungary, which gave them a shot at the World Cup via the play-offs.

He again was an unused substitute in the heartbreaking shootout defeat against Czech Republic before winning his 38th cap by starting in a 0-0 friendly draw against North Macedonia in May.

With Hallgrimsson's preference for playing with three centre-backs, Egan has certainly staked a claim for occupying one of those slots in the Nations League opener against Kosovo given his start to the season.

His case is strengthened by the fact that captain Collins is out injured, O'Brien has been limited to three appearances for Everton and O'Shea has been playing out of position at right-back for Ipswich Town.

The other centre-back options in the squad - new call-up Liam Kitching, Jimmy Dunne and James Abankwah - are inexperienced on the international stage.

Even if he does not start in Pristina, the condensed nature of the window and with a game against Austria sandwiched between two against Israel in 12 days, he is sure to see some game time for his country.

Given what he has gone through just to make it back to the top flight and into the Irish squad, Egan will fancy his chances of re-establishing himself as a starter for country as he did at club level.

articles.title: Hansi Flick, otro récord en su historia
articles.standfirst: Nunca había estado tanto tiempo en un banquillo de alta exigencia
articles.summary: Nunca había estado tanto tiempo en un banquillo de alta exigencia
articles.body: Hansi Flick ya está inmerso en su tercera temporada al frente del Barcelona y, curiosamente, nunca ha logrado completar tres años en un proyecto de máxima exigencia y con aspiraciones ambiciosas. Ni siquiera en sus anteriores experiencias de éxito, tanto en el Bayern de Múnich como en la selección alemana, disfrutó de un recorrido largo. Además, el Barcelona está plenamente convencido del trabajo del germano y el entrenador se siente orgulloso de formar parte de la entidad azulgrana. Y los resultados le amparan. Ha arrancado la campaña por todo lo alto, firmando pleno de triunfos y con un olfato goleador de escándalo. El pasado 13 de julio, Flick dio el pistoletazo de salida a su tercera temporada como entrenador del Barça. Hasta su llegada a la Ciudad Condal, sus dos grandes aventuras habían sido el Bayern de Múnich y la selección de Alemania. Su etapa en el conjunto de la Bundesliga empezó en noviembre de 2019, cuando asumió el cargo de manera interina tras la destitución de Niko Kovac. En su primer año, conquistó la Bundesliga, la Copa de Alemania y la Champions. Al curso siguiente amplió su palmarés con una nueva Bundesliga, la Supercopa de Alemania, la Supercopa de Europa y el Mundial de Clubes. Sin embargo, pese a tener contrato hasta 2023 y contar con el respaldo de los resultados, decidió abandonar el Bayern en el verano de 2021. Por lo tanto, firmó dos cursos y no completos. Pocas semanas después de dejar Múnich, la Federación Alemana anunció que Flick sería el relevo de Joachim Löw al frente de la selección. Debutó oficialmente en septiembre de 2021. Sin embargo, su aventura en el combinado germano tuvo un desenlace de dos años. El 10 de septiembre de 2023 fue destituido, después de una contundente derrota contra Japón. Por lo tanto, estuvo dos temporadas y la tercera arrancó con su adiós en el primer amistoso del curso. Ahora ya ha superado esa barrera de las dos temporadas y dos semanas. Y, salvo sorpresa mayúscula viendo cómo ha arrancado la campaña, el azulgrana completará la 26-27 en el Spotify Camp Nou. Tras unos meses alejado de los banquillos, el Barcelona apostó por él en el verano de 2024. Desde el primer momento, el entendimiento con Joan Laporta fue total y resultó decisivo para cerrar su incorporación. Para Flick, dirigir al Barcelona suponía cumplir uno de los grandes objetivos de su carrera. También conectó muy rápido con el equipo y con los seguidores, con un carácter muy cercano. Su adaptación fue inmediata. Pese a aterrizar en un contexto económico difícil, el técnico se identificó rápidamente con la filosofía futbolística del club. En dos temporadas y siete jornadas de LaLiga y una de la Champions, el balance es extraordinario. El conjunto azulgrana ya ha levantado cinco títulos. Ahora el gran objetivo de este tercer curso es conquistar la Champions, que se le ha resistido las dos campañas anteriores. De esta manera, Flick afronta una temporada muy especial y, a día de hoy, ya puede presumir de que el Barcelona es su proyecto más largo en la élite. La única etapa más longeva de su trayectoria como entrenador llegó a comienzos de la década de los 2000, cuando dirigió durante cinco temporadas al TSG 1899 Hoffenheim. Sin embargo, entonces el club militaba en la tercera división alemana y estaba muy lejos de la dimensión competitiva y mediática que representa el banquillo del Barcelona, del Bayern o de la selección. Este Barça ha iniciado la 26-27 rompiendo récords a todos los niveles, colectivos e inidividuales.

articles.title: Problema central en el Valencia: el 'informe Chris Smalling', en Paterna
articles.standfirst: El equipo ha quedado descompensado tras el mercado de verano con Gourlay, hay un detallado informe técnico del veterano central si bien Braulio puede abrir más ese mercado
articles.summary: El equipo ha quedado descompensado tras el mercado de verano con Gourlay, hay un detallado informe técnico del veterano central si bien Braulio puede abrir más ese mercado
articles.body: La planificación de Ron Gourlay en el Valencia ha dejado un panorama deportivo delicado. No hay más que verlo partido a partido y es la herencia que ha recibido Braulio Vázquez. El caso es que tras ver lo que sucede, la conclusión es que al equipo le falta un jugador clave en... defensa. Principalmente. Porque le faltan más puntos de refuerzo pero ante los pocos recursos de los que dispone el club en estos momentos las preferencias son la de un defensa con poso y solvencia. El equipo anda muy perdido en cuando a fortaleza defensiva. Sin un referente que haga la vida más tranquila y gane en confianza al resto de compañeros. El Valencia tiene tiempo para poder acometer ese perfil de jugador por el que tampoco se van a poder hacer dispendios. Uno de los jugadores que hay en el cajón del área de la secretaría técnica en la Ciudad deportiva de Paterna con todos los informes es el de un central libre, veterano y cuyas condiciones físicas son buenas porque no ha registrado lesiones importantes los últimos años. Se trata del inglés Chris Smalling (36 años que ha jugado entre otros en el Manchester United y en la Roma) que ahora mismo se encuentra sin equipo tras concluir la temporada, este verano pasado, en el Al-Fayha F. C. de la Liga Profesional Saudí. Se trata de una opción más de mercado que hay, a coste cero y que además forma parte del listado de jugadores que son ahora mismo agentes libres... El área deportiva del club tiene el nombre de este veterano como una de las mejores opciones dentro de los jugadores libres... si bien Braulio tiene ese tiempo de margen para poder encontrar un central 'sorpresa' que ofrezca ciertas garantías. Pero lo más destacado es que el Valencia acude casi sin dinero a este mercado de urgencias que será el de enero y sin capacidad de poder acometer una revolución. Por ello, una prioridad a día de hoy es la zaga y este defensa veterano cuenta con un buen informe en el área de la secretaría técnica de Paterna.

articles.title: El niño de 10 años que pesa 10 kilos por una enfermedad ultrarrara podrá jugar al fútbol con seguridad
articles.standfirst: Una excepción de la Federació Catalana de Futbol (FCF) permitirá a Luca poder jugar con chicos menores para evitar "riesgo crítico y evidente para su integridad física"
articles.summary: Una excepción de la Federació Catalana de Futbol (FCF) permitirá a Luca poder jugar con chicos menores para evitar "riesgo crítico y evidente para su integridad física"
articles.body: Un petición de 'change.org' de Iván Pascual García llamó la atención del mundo del fútbol: "¡Permitan que Luca (10 años, 10 kg,) juegue en una categoría segura!". Finalmente la Federació Catalana de Futbol (FCF) ha permitido a Luca, que sufre una alteración en el gen XRCC, competir con seguridad con el UE Castellnou. 'Infobae' informa que la FCF ha aceptado una excepción a las normas de edad para que Luca, que tendrá ficha sub-12, pueda competir con seguridad en la categoría sub-9. 'Regio7.cat' publica que "este hecho provocará que pueda ser convocado para los partidos, jugarlos y que los árbitros no pongan impedimento alguno. Eso sí, la Federación no podrá hacer nada en caso de que algún equipo del mismo grupo del Castellnou impugne un partido, lo que, con casi total seguridad, supondría la pérdida de los tres puntos". "A las autoridades de la Federació Catalana de Futbol (FCF): Mi hijo Luca tiene 10 años y padece una enfermedad ultra rara, siendo el único caso diagnosticado en España. Esta condición afecta directamente a su desarrollo físico: actualmente mide solo 1,07 metros y pesa 10,5 kg. Su gran pasión y su sueño es jugar al fútbol. Luca lleva cuatro años jugando en el UE Castellnou, donde está plenamente integrado con sus compañeros, pero al federarse el club esta temporada la normativa actual le impide seguir jugando con su equipo. Debido a su fragilidad ósea y muscular, obligarlo a competir contra niños de su misma edad biológica (que le triplican en peso y envergadura) supone un riesgo crítico y evidente para su integridad física. Por recomendación médica y puro sentido común, solicitamos a la FCF una adaptación excepcional de su licencia para que pueda jugar en una categoría inferior, con niños que se ajustan a su complexión física actual. Sin embargo, la Federación se ampara de forma estricta en el reglamento y le deniega esta adaptación, dejándolo fuera de los terrenos de juego. El fútbol base debe ser un espacio de educación, salud e inclusión, no de exclusión burocrática. Exigimos que la Federació Catalana de Futbol apruebe una excepción médica para Luca. Ningún niño debería quedarse sin jugar por culpa de una normativa que ignora la salud y la diversidad. Firma y comparte esta petición para que el fútbol sea, de verdad, para todos. ¡Muchisimas gracias!".

articles.title: Iñigo se queda 'sin equipo' para aprovechar el parón
articles.standfirst: La ausencia de 11 internacionales complica que el técnico pueda hacer su propia mini pretemporada
articles.summary: La ausencia de 11 internacionales complica que el técnico pueda hacer su propia mini pretemporada
articles.body: El Villarreal llega al larguísimo parón liguero con la tranquilidad que le otorgan las dos victorias consecutivas cosechadas ante la UD Levante y el Málaga CF. Un periodo que, en mitad del proceso de adaptación del equipo a los nuevos métodos que está implantando Iñigo Pérez, se veía como un momento ideal para incidir y trabajar en ellos. Pero la realidad es que la larga nómina de internacionales que han sido llamados por sus selecciones, impedirá al navarro aprovechar un periodo que parecía ideal para ello. Finalmente serán un total de once futbolistas del Villarreal los que vestirán la camiseta de su selección durante los compromisos internacionales del presente parón internacional. En esta caso los jugadores groguets que han sido citados por sus combinados nacionales para disputar distintos encuentros internacionales son: Santiago Mouriño (Uruguay), Alex Freeman (Estados Unidos), Nathan Saliba, Tajon Buchanan y Tani Oluwaseyi (Canadá), Georges Mikautadze (Georgia), Nicolas Pepe (Costa de Marfil), Pape Gueye (Senegal), Renato Veiga (Portugal) y Logan Costa (Cabo Verde). De la misma forma Carlos Maciá ha sido convocado por la Selección Española Sub-19 para unas jornadas de entrenamiento que se celebrarán del lunes 21 al jueves 24 en Marbella. Una extensa nómina que, unida a la lesión de Santi Comesaña, deja al Villarreal con ocho jugadores de campo del primer equipo al margen de los tres porteros. “En un parón tienes falta de control por los que se van y eso es algo que me genera estrés. Pero con lo que se queden trabajaremos situaciones posicionales, veremos a chicos del filial... hay partes positivas que queremos aprovechar” afirmaba con resignación el propio Iñigo tras la victoria ante el Levante. De esta forma, pocos conceptos podrá inculcar a gran parte del plantel tras quedar claro en este inicio de temporada que los amarillos todavía tiene mucho que mejorar. Pese a ello, el técnico ve positivo que haya un descanso en la competición: “El parón, tras dos victorias, no sé si es muy largo o muy corto. Pero yo prefiero parar, han sido semanas de carga emocional importante. Nos vamos a separar unas semanas y habrá un estado de relajación en el que nos quedaremos con lo bueno y desechemos lo tóxico”.

articles.summary: Faiq Bolkiah se ha quedado sin equipo tras terminar contrato con el Ratchaburi FC de la liga de Tailandia
articles.body: Faiq Bolkiah, el considerado el futbolista más rico del mundo, está sin equipo tras haber finalizado su contrato con el Ratchaburi FC de la liga de Tailandia. El futbolista de 28 años, que ha sido 6 veces internacional con Brunei y es el capitán de su selección, se formó en las canteras de AFC Newbury, Southampton, Chelsea y Leicester City y ha jugado a lo largo de su carrera para Marítimo, Chonburi y Ratchaburi. Faiq Bolkiah tienes más de 18.698 millones de euros de patrimonio por ser sobrino del Sultán de Brunei. Nció el 9 de mayo de 1998 en Los Ángeles (Estados Unidos) y es hijo del príncipe Jefri Bolkiah. Tiene una hermana gemela llamada Qiana y al menos 15 medio hermanos por parte de padre. Posee la ciudadanía tanto bruneana como estadounidense y se educó en el Reino Unido.

articles.title: Van Bommel, contundente en su llegada a Bélgica: "Podríais haber ganado el Mundial"
articles.standfirst: El neerlandés, nuevo seleccionador de los 'Diablos Rojos', quiso mandar un mensaje motivante a su plantilla
articles.summary: El neerlandés, nuevo seleccionador de los 'Diablos Rojos', quiso mandar un mensaje motivante a su plantilla
articles.body: El nuevo seleccionador de Bélgica, el neerlandés Mark Van Bommel, trasladó un mensaje de motivación a los Diablos Rojos en su primer encuentro con los futbolistas convocados para medirse contra Italia, Francia y Turquía en la Nations League, asegurando que los belgas podrían haber ganado el Mundial que se llevó España. "Creo que en el Mundial, con un poco más de suerte, deberíais haber llegado más lejos. Incluso podríais haberlo ganado", le dijo el técnico neerlandés a los 28 jugadores seleccionados en su primera convocatoria. Bélgica, con el francés Rudi Garcia como seleccionador, alcanzó los cuartos de final del Mundial de Estados Unidos, Canadá y México tras terminar primera de su grupo, con empates ante Egipto (1-1) e Irán (0-0) y una goleada frente a Nueva Zelanda (5-1). Ya en las eliminatorias, los Diablos Rojos vencieron a Senegal por 3-2 después de la prórroga en dieciseisavos y golearon por 4-1 a Estados Unidos en octavos. Su recorrido terminó en cuartos frente a España, que se impuso por 2-1 con un gol de Mikel Merino en el minuto 88, después de que Charles De Ketelaere hubiera igualado el tanto inicial de Fabián Ruiz, en un partido marcado por la lesión del meta Thibaut Courtois.

articles.standfirst: El brasileño reitera que el extremo debe ganar el Balón de Oro
articles.summary: El brasileño reitera que el extremo debe ganar el Balón de Oro
articles.body: Raphinha aprovecha cualquier comparecencia ante los medios para mostrarse tajante sobre quién tiene que ser el ganador del Balón de Oro. El internacional, en una entrevista a The Guardian, reitera, sin ningún atisbo de duda, que Lamine Yamal debe alzarse con el galardón por tres motivos claros: sus números, los títulos que ha ganado y su carisma. Raphinha deja clara su postura cuando se le pregunta si Lamine Yamal debe ser el nuevo Balón de Oro. "Sí, sin duda", afirma el capitán azulgrana. Además, asegura que, aunque no fuese compañero de equipo del canterano, seguiría pensando exactamente lo mismo. "Ganar el Balón de Oro depende de números individuales, títulos colectivos y la magia que tienes dentro del campo, el carisma. Son los puntos más importantes para llevarte este premio y Lamine Yamal lo tiene todos", asevera el internacional brasileño. El galardón se entregará el 26 de octubre en Londres. "Sus números son espectaculares, ha ganado dos títulos la temporada pasada con el Barcelona y el Mundial con España. Es uno de los jugadores más importantes del Barça y de la selección española. No hay ninguna duda. Se tiene que llevar el premio sí o sí. Es el principal candidato. Tiene que ganar", añade Raphinha.
