articles.title: Vote for Blue FCU's Fort Collins-area Football Player of Week (Week 4)
articles.summary: Vote for your Blue FCU Fort Collins-area Football Player of the Week, with nominees from Fort Collins, Timnath, Wellington and Windsor in Week 4.
articles.body:
The Coloradoan is proud to present another aspect of our weekly Athlete of the Week series, partnering with Blue Federal Credit Union to honor the best Fort Collins-area tackle football players throughout the fall 2026 season.

The weekly Fort Collins-area Football Player of the Week poll has five nominees, and fans can vote every Tuesday through Thursday at coloradoan.com/sports .

You can find the nominees and ballot below. Voting is open this week through 11:59 p.m. on Sept. 24 , with the winner announced Sept. 25.

Return to this page to see the official winner and a video of this week's Fort Collins-area Football Player of the Week atop the page.

Fans can nominate their favorite players (deadline: 11:59 p.m. every Sunday) and the Coloradoan sports staff will ultimately select the nominees each week.

If you have nominations for a future football Player of the Week, please send them via email to ChrisAbshire@coloradoan.com for consideration.

Meet the Blue FCU Football Player of the Week nominees and winner for Week 4 (Sept. 17-19):

Jackson Craig, Timnath QB: The Cubs needed just one half to get a running clock rolling against Niwot, and their senior QB led the way. Craig was again poised and efficient, going 6-of-8 passing with 143 yards and three touchdowns in the 49-0 win that has Timnath out to a 4-0 start this season.

Donovan Dumas, Fort Collins TE/LB: What a two-way game for the Lambkins junior. On defense, Dumas made a team-high nine tackles (one for loss) and added an interception. On offense, he was a mismatch, hauling in six catches for 123 yards and a TD in a blowout win at Erie.

Brayton Meglen, Wellington RB/KR: Meglen was absolutely electric in a 56-7 thrashing of 2A contender Strasburg. The Eagles junior carried the ball 21 times for 247 yards and five touchdowns (four in the first half) despite having two 50-plus yard TD runs called back by penalty.

Preston Mozer, Fort Collins WR : Mozer keeps looking like one of the best wide receivers in Colorado this season. The junior wideout had another big night, catching seven passes for 167 yards and two touchdowns, including an 82-yard strike to help keep the Lambkins unbeaten in a 56-9 win.

Robert Trotter Jr., Windsor QB: The Wizards got on the board with their first win of the season behind a strong offensive performance in a 42-0 win against Skyline. Trotter Jr. had a breakout game under center, going 11-of-14 with two TDs throwing the ball with another 20 rushing yards and a TD on the ground.

articles.title: Former Nebraska running back has strong day for the Kansas City Chiefs
articles.summary: Former Nebraska football running back Emmett Johnson is continuing to play at a high level for the Kansas City Chiefs.
articles.body:
Former Nebraska football running back Emmett Johnson is continuing to make waves with the Kansas City Chiefs . Chiefs coach Andy Reid said the team will give him the ball more after another solid performance in the Chiefs' win on Sunday.

Johnson had a big day for the Chiefs, doing a little bit of everything. He carried 15 times, averaging 7.5 yards per carry. He also contributed in the passing game, catching two passes for 20 yards. His longest catch was 12 yards.

Johnson also contributed on special teams. He also returned a kick for 34 yards. Overall, he had four total touches for 35 scrimmage yards. This was enough to impress his coach.

"I think Emmett will continue to get more snaps, and then that'll take a little bit of the load off Kenny (Walker)."

This is the second week in a row the former Nebraska standout has played a major role. The Chiefs are in good hands with Kenneth Walker III as the starting running back. That being said, Johnson is proving to be one of the most dependable backup running backs in the NFL.

Johnson's production is opening many eyes. However, it's nothing new for Huskers fans, who've seen it week after week.

articles.title: Notre Dame stays put in updated USA Today Sports NCAA Re-Rank
articles.summary: Notre Dame has remained consistent in the US LBM Coaches and AP polls. That rings true for the USA Today NCAA Re-Rank as well.
articles.body:
Notre Dame is No. 3 once again in this week's US LBM Coaches and Associated Press polls after Week 3 in college football.

Much like those rankings, the Fighting Irish have remained consistent in the latest USA Today Sports NCAA Re-Rank . For the second-straight week, Notre Dame is No. 2 and just behind top-ranked Texas .

Georgia , Ole Miss and Miami round out the top of USAT's re-rank.

See photos from Notre Dame's win over the Michigan State Spartans

The Irish are coming off a 27-10 win over Michigan State on Saturday. The Spartans are currently No. 63 in the re-rank list.

Notre Dame (3-0) will face Purdue (1-2) this weekend. The Boilermakers are 95th in the re-rank.
